title: Four Ways to Know

source.quote: Behavioral diagnosis is the most important of the four. The other three act as checks upon it.

setting: Tuesday, 2pm. A tiny typo in Noah's report got fixed before anyone outside the team even saw it.

L1.line: I'm so sorry, I'll fix it right now, I promise, it won't happen again...
cues: voice high and fast, shoulders hunched (behavioural)
coworkers immediately start reassuring him like he's fragile (social)
he's mentioned teachers calling out his mistakes in front of the class (historical)
he says "it's like I'm back in Mrs Carrow's class" (phenomenological)
L1.question: Behavioural, social, historical and phenomenological diagnosis all point somewhere. Which ego state is Noah actually in?

options.text: Adult - he's just being thorough about fixing a real mistake
options.feedback: A real mistake calls for a calm, specific fix; none of the four diagnoses here point to measured here-and-now problem-solving - they all point to something older.

options.text: Parent - he's holding himself to a standard
options.feedback: Close, in that a Parental standard is probably driving this from inside him - but the behaviour, the response he's pulling from others, and his own words all describe the state that standard is aimed at, not that state itself.

Right. Hunched posture and fast apology (behavioural), coworkers reassuring him like he's small (social), teachers calling him out as a child (historical), and his own "back in Mrs Carrow's class" (phenomenological) - all four point to Child, which is Berne's standard for a complete diagnosis.

Berne said a complete diagnosis uses all four checks together, and here they agree, not conflict - when behavioural, social, historical and phenomenological evidence all land in the same place, that's as confirmed as a diagnosis gets.

L1.lesson: Behavioural diagnosis is the most important and should come first, but checking it against social, historical and phenomenological evidence turns a guess into a diagnosis; getting two or more of Berne's four ways to agree is what makes a call reliable rather than a hunch from tone of voice alone.

L2.intro: The typo really was tiny. What do you say to Noah?

beats.line: I'm so sorry, I'll fix it right now, I promise, it won't happen again...

options.text: It's fine, don't worry about it, I'll just fix it myself.
options.outcome: Noah relaxes but still looks small. "Okay... thank you." The pattern isn't challenged, just soothed.
options.lesson: Nurturing Parent calms the moment, which matches what his Child is braced for - comfortable, but it keeps the transaction exactly where his Child expects it to land.

options.text: It's one typo, Noah - this isn't Mrs Carrow's class.
options.outcome: Noah blinks, laughs a little. "Ha... yeah. Sorry. I mean - thanks." Something shifts.
options.lesson: Naming the historical echo directly, from Adult, gives Noah's own Adult something to recognize and step into - this kind of cross can interrupt an old pattern instead of just soothing it.

options.text: You really don't need to apologize like that for every little thing.
options.outcome: Noah's shoulders hunch further. "Sorry - sorry, you're right, I'll stop." The apology just grew a layer.
options.lesson: A correction aimed at his Child from Parent gets received by his Child exactly like every other correction always has - it feeds the pattern instead of breaking it.

options.text: Honestly, it's not a big deal, these things happen to everyone.
options.outcome: Noah nods, still tense. "Right. Yeah. Sorry." True, but it doesn't land yet.
options.lesson: Good Adult content, but it's generic reassurance rather than anything specific to Noah's actual pattern - true, but it doesn't address what's actually happening for him right now.

fields.label: Draw the vectors for Noah's apology, and for Dana's best response.
In under 60 words: name Berne's four ways to diagnose an ego state, and say which one Noah's own words ("back in Mrs Carrow's class") provide.

echo.setting: 72 hours later: Dana catches herself over-apologizing to a barista for a wrong order.
echo.line: Oh my god, I'm so sorry, that's totally my fault, I should have said it clearer...
echo.shape: same four-diagnoses shape as L1, turned on the player
